subject: Service fit decision matrix and swap plan — post-demo recap
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PulseHealth demo — deployment fit recap and next steps

Hi Samir — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side and the two decision tracks we discussed: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem).

Summary of what you shared:
- Latency target: 120ms p95 for patient-facing flows (avg token lengths ~40).
- Data residency: Production PHI must remain in VPC or be encrypted with customer KMS; non-PHI test traffic can run on hosted.
- Existing footprint: Current in-house cluster (NVIDIA A40s) serving via a custom API; 50k requests/day with 2 bursts/week.
- CapEx constraint: team is sensitive to upfront spend and would prefer consumption or a phased reserved model.

Recommended decision matrix items (what to consider):
1) Short-term (30–60 days): Keep current cluster in place, use Redwood Hosted for staging and gradual offload (can replicate traffic slices).
2) Mid-term (90–180 days): Evaluate Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) if steady-state throughput and latency goals are met; reserved reduces unit cost versus Hosted.
3) Long-term: Private VPC or on-prem only if regulatory signoff requires full customer-managed network and HSM/KMS integration.

Action items we promised:
- Redwood: deliver a tailored decision matrix and a Swap Plan (lift-and-shift + fallbacks) that maps your current endpoints to Hosted/Dedicated/Private variants. See attached initial checklist (pulse-deploy-checklist.xlsx).
- PulseHealth: confirm which workloads are PHI (obligatory for Private) and approximate steady-state QPS and peak burst characteristics.
- Procurement: loop in estimated SOW/commit numbers if you want quotes for Dedicated.

If it helps, Karthik and I can run a short traffic-profile analysis on a one-week sample and return a cost/latency projection for Hosted vs 2 Dedicated shapes.

Best,
David

--
David Kim

David — thanks for the clear recap and for the checklist. A couple of clarifications from our side: we appreciate the phased approach. A few specifics: 

1) PHI tagging: the only PHI flows are "clinical summarization" and "medication reconciliation" endpoints — roughly 30% of total requests but 60% of sensitive latency requirements.
2) Our in-house A40 cluster is stable but we lack a robust KV-cache strategy. Switching infrastructure this quarter is politically hard — engineering prefers a blue/green migration where we can fallback to the legacy cluster.
3) Procurement asked for a simple decision tree: if Redwood Dedicated reduces per-token cost by >30% vs Hosted for our profile and meets p95 SLA, we will consider a 12-month commitment.

Can you include in the decision matrix: a clear rollback plan (routing back to A40s), how KV cache warm-up will be handled, and a checklist of KMS/HSM integration steps for the Private option? Also include a stub SOW/ballpark for a 50k req/day average with burst to 150k.

Subject: Decision matrix draft & swap plan next actions — PulseHealth

Samir / Procurement — attaching the draft decision matrix and the swap plan (see links below). High level: we built the matrix against your stated constraints (120ms p95, PHI endpoints flagged, traffic profile assumptions). Key calls we made in the draft: 

- Hosted API: fastest to try (no infra changes) — recommended for staging and non-PHI workloads; estimated cost (hosted) = ~$0.085/token for your sample (see projection).
- Dedicated: recommended if you commit 12 months at ~40% lower per-token cost; meets latency target on tested shapes with conservative kernel selection. Requires a 30% commit to get to cost band.
- Private VPC / On-prem: only if compliance requires customer-managed KMS/HSM; engineering effort ~6–8 weeks for HSM integration + network validation.

Swap plan highlights:
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): mirror traffic for 10% of requests to Redwood Hosted for profiling; no routing cutover.
- Phase 1 (30 days): route read-only and non-PHI traffic to Hosted; maintain A40s as primary for PHI endpoints.
- Phase 2 (60–90 days): if Dedicated is approved, provision a dedicated pool and shift burst traffic; KV cache warm-up policy: progressive prefix seeding over 72 hours with a warm-hit threshold metric.
- Rollback triggers: any 10% spike in error rate or sustained p95 > 200ms for 1 hour -> immediate rollback to legacy endpoints.

Attachments (stubs): pulse-deploy-checklist.xlsx, redwood-mop-v1.pdf

Links:
- Decision matrix (preview): https://drive.redwood.com/s/shared/pulse/decision-matrix-draft
- Swap plan (doc): https://drive.redwood.com/s/shared/pulse/swap-plan-v0.1

Next steps (concrete):
1) Samir: confirm PHI endpoint list and give a one-week traffic sample CSV to us by Mon 21 Sep.
2) Procurement: indicate whether you want a 12-month Dedicated quote or to start with Hosted consumption only. If Dedicated, provide expected commit % (we modeled at 30%).
3) Internal: Karthik to run profiler and share results by Mon 21 Sep. Marissa to produce SOW draft by Mon EOD.

We're available for a 30-min follow-up on Tue 22 Sep to walk the matrix and SOW with procurement.

Thanks,
David
